crop.notes: Full item, from headline 'THE ALLEN-GALLAGHER FIGHT. It Takes Place To-day.' to the end.

ocr.notes: Transcript matches the image; the subhead 'It Takes Place To-day' is omitted.

summary.suggested: The Missouri Republican reported that Tom Allen's prize fight with Gallagher would take place that day at a secret spot within sixty miles of St. Louis, with Patsy Reardon, newly arrived from Ireland, seconding Allen.

metadata.notes: Masthead reads 'The Missouri Republican—St. Louis, February 23, 1869' (Tuesday), so it is the same paper as the St. Louis Republican. The item is in a middle column, near the bottom. The paper was called the Missouri Republican on that date, so it is filed under that name rather than 'St. Louis Republican'.

facts.fact: Allen's prize fight with Gallagher was to take place on Feb. 23, 1869, at a point within sixty miles of St. Louis; the exact spot was kept secret
places: within sixty miles of St. Louis

facts.fact: Patsy Reardon, 'the hero of sixteen victories', recently arrived from Ireland, was to second Allen against Gallagher

notes: The current summary calls the opponent 'Felix Gallagher'. The article gives no first name; this was the Charley Gallagher fight of Feb. 23, 1869. The Bill Ryall line is about a different person and is left out of the facts.
